Items.Authors: H. Philip Stahl, Tomasz Lis, David Smith, Ron Eng, Conrad Wells
Items.Title: Thermal Modulation Test (TMT) method and recent results in the mini-Precision Thermal Control (PTC) testbed
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) requires an ultra-stable optical telescope. Critical to this need is thermos-optical stability of the primary mirror assembly. To meet this need, MSFC’s Center for Mirror System Characterization and Acceptance Testing has developed and demonstrated a picometer sensitivity milli-kelvin thermal modulation test (TMT) method that can measure a mirror’s thermal response to thermal stimuli with a noise floor of 0.2 to 0.5 picometers per mK. Additionally, MSFC has build an 80-cm mini-PTC (Precision Thermal Control) testbed with 25-zones of active thermal control. This paper reviews the TMT method, mini-PTC capability and presents test results from ULE® and borosilicate mirrors.

Items.Authors: Matthew East
Items.Title: Thermal testing of stable telescope mirrors
Items.Abstract: Detecting and characterizing Earth-like planets around distant stars requires exceptionally stable telescopes. NASA's "Critical Technologies for Large Telescopes" project advances essential technologies for the Habitable Worlds Observatory, including the demonstration of stable mirror technologies. This paper focuses on strategies for managing the thermal mass of mirrors to enhance thermal-optical stability for the Observatory's primary mirror segments. It includes testing of two lightweight mirrors to evaluate their thermal performance. This hardware will be one of the first test subjects evaluated using new stable environment facilities at the NASA GSFC Ultra-Stable Structures Laboratory. Future goals include demonstrations of millikelvin-class thermal stability and picometer-class optical stability relevant to the Habitable Worlds Observatory.

Items.Authors: Ananya Sahoo, Christopher Mendillo, Thaddeus Potter, Kuravi Hewawasam, Jason Martel
Items.Title: Thermal, structural, and optical analysis of balloon-borne coronagraphic imaging system
Items.Abstract: We present a thermal, structural and optical performance analysis for the Planetary Imaging Coronagraph Testbed Using a Recoverable Experiment for Debris Disks (PICTURE-D), a NASA balloon-borne observatory designed to image dust and debris disks around nearby stars in reflected visible light. Key components of PICTURE-D include a 60 cm off-axis telescope, a vector vortex coronagraph to suppress stellar light, and two MEMS based deformable mirrors for wavefront sensing and control. The balloon flight environment presents key challenges to the stability of the wavefront required for imaging. Low ambient temperature and pressure induce thermo-mechanical deformation of the observatory and limit the performance of the coronagraph. Using an integrated finite element model of observatory plus the coronagraph, we model the thermo-structural evolution of the observatory and assess the coronagraphic performance of the instrument.

Items.Authors: Wouter van Straalen
Items.Title: THESIS: development of a goniometric spectro-polarimeter for planetary surface analogue measurements
Items.Abstract: In the study of planetary bodies, spectrometry of reflected light is used to characterize the composition of planetary surfaces. However, light polarization, which can be studied in addition to the spectrum, also carries information about the microscopic structure of planetary surfaces. The reflected polarization can be connected to the grain size, porosity, signatures of living organisms, and more. To expand our knowledge on the applications of spectro-polarimetry in planetary surface characterization, the AgSPARROW instrument is being developed at TU Delft to measure the full Stokes spectro-polarimetric signature of light (350 – 3500 nm) reflected from planetary surface analogue samples at various phase angles. The study will focus on investigating polarization signatures that can reveal information about surface structures which is inaccessible with only spectral measurements. In this talk, we will present the design, capabilities, and the first measurements of the instrument.

Items.Authors: J. Duane Gibson, William Goble, Kenneth Duffek, Dallan Porter, Jerome Musselman, Thomas Gansheimer
Items.Title: Time- and frequency-domain analysis of high-resolution mount tracking data at the MMTO
Items.Abstract: High-resolution telemetry data (100 Hz) from the MMT Observatory telescope mount, including altitude, azimuth, and rotator axes, are analyzed in the time and frequency domains to evaluate tracking performance. Data are sampled for 2 minutes every 10 minutes during active observing. Using Python tools, including Welch power spectral density (PSD) estimates, data are evaluated over multiple years across various telescope configurations (secondary mirrors, instruments, counterweight settings). The analysis employs dual methods: time-domain standard deviation regression and frequency-domain PSD analysis, with directional separation to distinguish upward/downward motion in elevation and clockwise/counterclockwise motion in azimuth and rotation. Results indicate overall smooth tracking, with identifiable trends suggesting possible operational improvements. These tools help assess how environmental and mechanical factors impact tracking performance, supporting future upgrades.

Items.Authors: Lisa-Marie Mazzolo, Benoit Neichel, Guido Agapito, Arseniy Kuznetsov, Fabio Rossi, Cédric Plantet, Carlo Felice Manara, Romain Fetick, Alice Concas, Joël Vernet, Olivier Hainaut, Thomas Bierwirth, Giulia Carlà, Jean-Francois Sauvage, Michele Cirasuolo, Carlos Correia, Cédric Taissir Héritier, Thierry Fusco
Items.Title: TipTop: a fast and versatile analytical tool for AO PSF prediction
Items.Abstract: TipTop is a fast and versatile analytical tool designed to predict Adaptive Optics (AO) Point Spread  Functions (PSFs) for any observing mode and any set of atmospheric conditions. Built on a  Fourier-domain formulation of the residual phase, it combines high-order and low-order error  contributions to efficiently explore diverse system configurations. TipTop supports multiple  applications, including support for exposure-time calculators, observation preparation, AO system  design, and the selection of optimal Natural Guide Star (NGS) asterisms. The tool has been  extensively validated against several end-to-end simulation codes and is already used for various VLT  instruments. It is also being adopted by multiple facilities and instrument teams in preparation for the  ELT. Ongoing developments investigate TipTop-inspired approaches for PSF reconstruction  (Kuznetsov et al. (subm.)) and new user-oriented capabilities.  More info: https://astro-tiptop-services.github.io/astro-tiptop-services/

Items.Authors: Natalie R. Fullerman, Joseph M. Howard
Items.Title: Tools for non-sequential ray tracing through segmented telescopes for Habitable Worlds Observatory
Items.Abstract: Architectures are currently being explored for NASA’s upcoming flagship mission, Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO). Similar to James Webb Space Telescope, the primary mirrors are being designed as segmented rather than monolithic. This introduces the need for non-sequential ray tracing in an optical model. In order to make this conversion process more efficient, a series of macros can be written in CODE V. The programs will turn surfaces from sequential to non-sequential, insert the appropriate number of segments, and automatically generate the required geometries for each part. Considerations include:  •Segment shape   •Gap size between segments   •Segment numbers & orientation composing the full mirror

Items.Authors: Ahmed Soliman, Stuart Shaklan, John Mather, Eliad Peretz, Zahra Ahmed, Manan Arya, Harsh Bhundiya, Aman Chandra, Jessie Christiansen, Mario Damiano, Richard Dekany, Juliana Garcia-Mejia, Christine Gregg, Markus Kasper, Jennifer Lopez, David Miller, Rhonda Morgan, Jalo Nousiainen, Sergio Pellegrino, Peter Plavchan, William Sanchez, Aniket Sanghi, Jonathan Sauder, Andrew Szentgyorgyi, Jamila Taaki, Ronald Turner, Amber Young, Aiden Zelakiewicz, Sungeun Jeon, Dmitry Savransky, Shannon Brown, Jonathan Arenberg, Mark Silver, Christophe Lovis, Michel Mayor
Items.Title: Toward a hybrid ground-space exoplanet observatory: summary of Caltech Keck Institute for Space Studies (KISS) program
Items.Abstract: The hybrid integration of ground-based telescopes with space-based optical components has the potential for unprecedented observational precision, opening new horizons for scientific discoveries in astronomy. We focus on the first hybrid ground-space observatory dedicated to the search for life beyond Earth-a top scientific priority in modern astronomy. In this talk, we present, on behalf of the KISS team, the findings of our recent study supported by the Caltech KISS program, which outlines a clear implementation plan and workflow for designing and deploying a shared 99 m orbiting starshade to work with large ground-based telescopes equipped with adaptive optics (AO) such as the 39 m ELT, 30 m TMT, 24 m GMT, and 10 m Keck to directly image Earth-like planet around a Sun-like star. This approach provides high-contrast imaging and high-resolution spectroscopy, enabling the search for potential biosignatures such as oxygen and water.

Items.Authors: Anusha Pai Asnodkar, Nemanja Jovanovic, Yoo Jung Kim, Harry-Dean Kenchington-Goldsmith, Ahmed Sanny, Michael Fitzgerald, Dimitri Mawet, Pradip Gatkine
Items.Title: Tricouplers for nulling interferometry with photonic integrated circuits
Items.Abstract: Photonic integrated circuits (PICs) offer a promising platform for space-based nulling interferometry. However, their design and manufacturing precision are insufficient for the stringent requirements of exoplanet detection. We investigate the nulling capabilities of photonic tricouplers, devices composed of 3 equal-width waveguides to produce achromatic nulls upon beam combination by virtue of their symmetric construction. In the lab, we characterize null depths, splitting ratios, and light leakage in monochromatic light (1.55 μm) as well as chromatic effects from thermo-optic phase shifters in H-band light for tricouplers on a planar silica-on-silicon platform. In simulation, we identify avenues for optimizing the tradeoff between deep achromatic nulling, exoplanet signal, and wavefront sensing. Our ongoing efforts towards maturation of PICs will support scalable testing and deployment of high-contrast technologies for future missions, such as the Habitable Worlds Observatory.

Items.Authors: Yuhei Takagi, Yosuke Minowa, Shin Oya, Yoshito Ono, Hirofumi Okita, Richard C. Y. Chou, Shiang-Yu Wang, Po-Chieh Yu
Items.Title: ULTIMATE-Subaru: concept and the strategy of the calibration process of the adaptive secondary mirror and the wavefront sensor
Items.Abstract: We present the functionality and the performance verification plan of the adaptive secondary mirror and the wavefront sensor of the ULTIMATE-Subaru project, which is the next-generation facility instrument for the Subaru Telescope. A test tower will be used to evaluate the surface of the mirror, and an optical platform is designed and installed on this tower to test both the adaptive secondary mirror and the wavefront sensor. The detailed concept and the strategy of the calibration and the verification of the adaptive secondary and the wavefront sensor will be described in this presentation.

Items.Authors: Rita F. Sonka, Karwan Rostem, Jake Connors, Shannon Duff, Johannes Hubmayr, Tuomas Puurtinen, Elmer H. Sharp, Edward J. Wollack
Items.Title: Ultra-low noise transition edge sensors with high pixel-filling fraction for far-infrared astronomy
Items.Abstract: We present progress in absorber-coupled ultra-low noise transition edge sensor (TES) bolometers for suborbital and space-borne far-infrared instruments. The TESs are fabricated on a thin (~200 nm thick) silicon nitride membrane with compact (~50 µm long) suspending phononic-filtering legs. These filters’ non-uniform leg geometry (e.g. stubs) creates coherent phonon reflections within the leg, reducing the thermal conductance (G) more than straight uniform legs could in the same space. This enables high pixel filling fraction [>0.7] of the focal plane and ultra-low noise measured at ~3x10^-19 W/rtHz at 10 Hz and 50 mK bath temperature (Tb) with TESes biased to half their normal resistance. We present measurements of noise and responsivity versus Tb for pixels with different phononic filters. We also investigate the transport process in these low-dimensional mesoscopic structures by comparing the phononic filter G with predictions from elastic wave and boundary limited scattering models.

Items.Authors: Randall L. McEntaffer, Fabien Grise, Brian Fleming, Nicholas Kruczek, Kevin France, Stephan McCandliss, Mackenzie Carlson, Emily Witt, Drew Miles
Items.Title: Ultraviolet diffraction grating development for Habitable Worlds Observatory and related missions
Items.Abstract: The Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) will provide UV spectroscopy to accomplish a number of science goals from composition of planet-forming disks to the evolution of ionizing radiation over cosmic time. Obtaining the required spectrograph performance in spectral resolving power, scattered light control, and diffraction efficiency will involve maturation of key technologies specific to UV gratings. In preparation for HWO developments, a Technology Maturation Plan for UV gratings has been submitted to NASA. This plan concentrates on maturing high-efficiency echelle gratings, aberration-correcting gratings, and low-blaze-angle gratings. It outlines necessary improvements for establishing appropriate metrology and characterization instrumentation and facilities. Furthermore, the utilization of high-performance UV coatings on gratings will be studied. Here, we present an overview of progress along the maturation plan, with details on the milestones, schedule, and technology highlights.

Items.Authors: Justin Payan, Noemi Barbagli, Nihar B. Shah, Rodrigo A. Carrasco, Ignacio Toledo, Sergio Martín
Items.Title: Uncertainty-aware ground-based telescope observation scheduling at ALMA
Items.Abstract: We study the problem of scheduling under changing environmental conditions in ground-based telescopes. Observations queued in service mode have strict requirements on stochastic environmental conditions like the weather. Although observatories can compute forecasts, conditions often deviate from these forecasts. Existing approaches do not anticipate these deviations, leading to reduced efficiency. Our approach selects observations by taking into account the uncertainty around the forecasts. Using data from ALMA, we show that our approach improves balance across funding agencies and increases completion rates for high-priority projects. We developed this scheduling algorithm for the Joint ALMA Observatory, but it is potentially applicable to any ground-based telescope operated in service mode, such as ESO’s VLT and ELT, or NRAO’s VLA and ngVLA.

Items.Authors: Mees Altena
Items.Title: Unified LOFAR proposal and project management with TULP and NARCIS
Items.Abstract: LOFAR 2.0 operations are structured around projects, ranging from one-off observations to long-term multi-epoch programmes. We have developed two open source applications to enable science users and system operators to track projects through the system. Our new proposal tool, TULP, and project management and resource monitoring tool, NARCIS. TULP and NARCIS are fully integrated with our operational system. TULP supports the full proposal flow, NARCIS, provides information on resource usage by observations and processing, for granted projects.    We give an overview of the architecture of TULP and NARCIS, and how they embed into LOFAR, integrating with telescope management, pipeline execution, resource and visibility calculators, and the archive. We show how the functionality of the tools matches user flows, both from the PI and telescope operator point of view, and how the design of the tools meets current or short-term user needs, while being extensible for the future.

Items.Authors: Maren Cosens, Patricio Schurter, Nicholas P. Konidaris, Gwen C. Rudie, Andrew B. Newman, Leon Aslan, Robert Barkhouser, Christoph Birk, Julia E. Brady, Tyson Hare, Stephen C. Hope, Charlie Hull, Daniel D. Kelson, Gerrad Killion, Alicia Lanz, Solange V. Ramírez, William Schoenell, Stephen A. Smee, Jason E. Williams
Items.Title: Update on the slicer IFU for the Magellan InfraRed Multi-Object Spectrograph (MIRMOS)
Items.Abstract: We will present an update of the slicer IFU for the Magellan InfraRed Multi-Object Spectrograph (MIRMOS), a planned next generation multi-object and integral field spectrograph for the 6.5m Magellan telescopes at Las Campanas Observatory. MIRMOS will perform R~3700 spectroscopy over a simultaneous wavelength range of 0.886 - 2.404um. The integral field mode of operation for MIRMOS will be achieved via an image slicer style integral field unit (IFU) located on a linear stage to facilitate movement into the beam during use or storage while operating in multi-object mode. The IFU will provide an ~18”x26” field of view (FoV) made up of 0.84”x26” slices. This will be the largest FoV IFS operating at these wavelengths from either the ground or space, making MIRMOS an ideal instrument for a wide range of science cases.

Items.Authors: Antonio Matta-Gómez, Jorge Quintero Nehrkorn, Horacio Rodríguez Delgado, Juan Carlos Trelles Arjona, Carlos Quintero Noda, Silvia Regalado Olivares, Jonai Bienes, Patricia Gómez González, Manuel Collados
Items.Title: Updating the Control Software of the Multi-Channel GRIS Spectropolarimeter for Simultaneous observations.
Items.Abstract: The GREGOR Infrared Spectrograph (GRIS) has fundamentally evolved into a multi-channel system for simultaneous magnetic field mapping. To handle the complex coordination of up to three detectors, the control software, POLAR, was updated to a new version called POLAR 2.0. This upgrade features two major innovations. First, observation sequencing replaced legacy indexed lists with a Finite State Machine (FSM) approach, enhancing clarity and scalability. Second, the architecture became modular and distributed, allowing framegrabbers to operate across multiple computers for high throughput. Crucially, hard real-time synchronization is achieved by decoupling network tasks from the dedicated synchronization hardware, ensuring temporal coherence across all multi-rate detectors for the future commissioning of the instrument's third spectral channel.

Items.Authors: Anton Neisius, Elodie Choquet, Vincent Chambouleyron, Arthur Vigan
Items.Title: Upgrade of the MITHiC Testbed for intensity and phase control
Items.Abstract: High-contrast imaging for direct exoplanet detection is limited by stellar brightness and wavefront errors. Coronagraphy and wavefront control help reduce these effects and enable contrast levels compatible with current testbeds and future missions such as the Roman Space Telescope.  Within this framework, the MITHiC testbed at the Laboratoire d’Astrophysique de Marseille is being upgraded with a new Spatial Light Modulator (SLM) used as a deformable mirror. It complements the existing setup, which includes a Classic Lyot Coronagraph and a first SLM enabling phase and amplitude control to optimize the dark-hole region. We also implement the Zernike wavefront sensor (ZELDA) to correct low-order aberrations.  This contribution presents recent progress on the MITHiC upgrade and initial results, highlighting its role as a versatile platform for developing advanced high-contrast imaging techniques.

Items.Authors: Tom Moynihan, Ana Jenkins
Items.Title: Utilising the Tensor Core Correlator for intra-station correlation in SKA-Low
Items.Abstract: The Square Kilometre Array Low Frequency Telescope (SKA-Low) is a large radio telescope under construction in Western Australia, consisting of stations of 256 dual-polarisation antennas. Their signals must be cross-correlated to calculate calibration solutions for each station. The Monitoring, Control and Calibration Subsystem (MCCS) performs this correlation, receiving digitised and channelised data from 16 Tile Processing Modules per station. This paper describes the integration of the Tensor Core Correlator (TCC) into the MCCS data-acquisition pipeline as a replacement for xGPU. TCC provides significantly higher throughput, increasing the number of concurrent correlations per GPU from four to eleven. This improvement de-conficts correlation operations for the current 16-station Array Assembly 1 (AA1) deployment and reduces the required compute for the forthcoming 68-station Array Assembly 2 (AA2).

Items.Authors: Abigail White, Charlie Conroy, Daniel Fabricant
Items.Title: Viaspec spectrograph and fiber positioner: enabling precision stellar spectroscopy
Items.Abstract: The Via Project will constrain the nature of dark matter by measuring disturbances within cold stellar streams, characterize the faintest dwarf galaxies, and map cold gas structure in the Milky Way halo. Achieving these science goals requires radial velocity accuracy of 100 m/s. To accomplish this, Via will deploy twin multi-object, fiber-fed spectrographs on the 6.5-meter MMT and Magellan/Clay telescopes. The Via instrument has two major subsystems: the fiber positioning system (FPS) and the bench spectrograph, Viaspec. The FPS includes 576 theta-phi robotic positioners and 60 fiducials, providing coverage across a 1-degree field of view. Optical fibers route light from the focal plane through the fiber chain to Viaspec - an R = 15,000 spectrograph operating over a narrow wavelength range of 5050 - 5950 Å. In this poster, we present details of the FPS design and our evaluation of the focal ratio degradation, throughput, and scrambling of the fiber optics.

Items.Authors: Gregory A. Barrick, Arturo Lopez-Ariste, Jean-François Donati, Marielle Lacombe, Sébastien Baratchart, Driss Kouach, Emilien Carrie, Nicolas Striebig, François Olchewlsky, Michel Dupieux, Julien Garnier, Tom Vermeulen, Cam Wipper
Items.Title: VISION-CFHT/Wenaokeao: combining the power of SPIRou and ESPaDOnS at CFHT
Items.Abstract: The VISION-CFHT/Wenaokeao instrument being built at IRAP/OMP in Toulouse, France will combine the ESPaDOnS and SPIRou instruments at CFHT. Both instruments provide full, broad-band spectroscopy in a single exposure with ESPaDOnS in the visible (360-1050 nm, resolution 68,000 to 81,000) and SPIRou in the near-infrared (970-2493 nm, resolution 65,000), as well as polarimetric analysis of the incoming light. In addition, SPIRou provides precision RV accuracy at the level of 2 m/s.  The new instrument will provide three observing modes: SPIRou only, ESPaDOnS only, and SPIRou and ESPaDOnS simultaneously. The third mode is what makes VISION-CFHT/Wenaokeao unique by taking simultaneous high-resolution spectra over the entire wavelength range from 370 to 2500 nm. This paper describes the design, challenges, and expected performance of this new instrument.  VISION-CFHT/Wenaokeao is based on the VISION instrument on the Télecope Bernard Lyot (TBL) at the Observatoire du Pic du Midi.

Items.Authors: Jonathan St-Antoine
Items.Title: VROOMM: development update on a high-precision radial velocity spectrograph for the Observatoire du Mont-Mégantic
Items.Abstract: We present a development update on VROOMM, a high-resolution (360–930 nm) échelle spectrograph for precision radial velocity measurements at the 1.6-m telescope of the Observatoire du Mont-Mégantic (OMM), Québec, Canada. Since our initial design, the frontend optical system is finalized and under fabrication and assembly. The backend optical design is complete, with elements under construction, and the spectrograph mechanical design is in progress. A detector engineering cryostat is being built to evaluate the unique 4K photon-counting EMCCD by e2v, enabling 100–200 m/s precision on very faint targets (rsdss = 19–20). Facility preparations at OMM, including integration, guiding system tests, and a dedicated scheduling system, are underway to accommodate VROOMM as the primary instrument.

Items.Authors: Mirko Colapietro, Salvatore Savarese, Pietro Schipani, Francesco Perrotta, Sergio D'Orsi, Laurent Marty, Giulio Capasso, Simone Di Filippo, Demetrio Magrin, Jacopo Farinato, Gabriele Umbriaco, Stefano Covino, Pierfrancesco Rossettini, Paolo Spanò, Raffaele Tomelleri
Items.Title: VSTPOL: instrument assembly, verification, and test results
Items.Abstract: VSTPOL is a new polarimetric module designed to extend the capabilities of the 2.6-m VLT Survey Telescope (VST) by enabling wide-field optical imaging polarimetry.  The instrument replaces the existing electro-opto-mechanical system positioned between the primary mirror cell and the wide-field imaging camera (OmegaCAM) with a redesigned assembly that integrates: a linear translation mechanism to switch between the imaging and polarimetric modes; a rotating unit, consisting of two plano-spherical lenses with a linear polarizer inserted between them, allowing continuous tracking to compensate for field rotation by synchronizing its motion with that of OmegaCAM.  This paper presents the complete assembly, integration and verification process of VSTPOL, detailing the design solutions adopted to meet the system requirements and the test results.  The instrument is now ready for installation at the telescope expected by the end of 2026.

Items.Authors: Pietro Schipani, Stefano Covino, Frans Snik, Mirko Colapietro, Francesco Perrotta, Salvatore Savarese, Simone Di Filippo, Stefano Bagnulo, Pierluigi Bellutti, Giulio Capasso, Enrico Cappellaro, Massimo Cappi, Gianluca Castignani, Sergio D'Orsi, Jacopo Farinato, Olivier Hainaut, Damien Hutsemekers, Konrad Kuijken, Antonio M. Magalhaes, Demetrio Magrin, Marcella Marconi, Laurent Marty, Ferdinando Patat, Elena Pian, Fabio Rigamonti, Vincenzo Ripepi, Pierfrancesco Rossettini, Alain Smette, Paolo Spanò, Raffaele Tomelleri, Gabriele Umbriaco, Gijs Verdoes Kleijn, Alex van Vorstenbosch
Items.Title: VSTPOL: status and development of the wide-field polarimetric upgrade for the VST Telescope
Items.Abstract: The VSTPOL project will transform the VST into one of the first wide-field polarimetric large facility for high-precision, large-area surveys. Building on the VST’s 2.6-m, 1deg FoV, VSTPOL adds a new optomechanical module enabling polarimetry across the full field. Science goals include studying polarized emission from Galactic and extragalactic sources, and performing time-domain polarimetry of transients; its location near CTAO-South enables rapid polarimetric follow-up of CTAO sources. The polarimetric device, integrating a dedicated filter within the field corrector, has been fully realized after design and system integration. Laboratory tests show compliance with requirements. Work continues on control software, calibration tools, and AIV preparation. Installation at Paranal is planned for 2026, followed by system verification, on-sky commissioning, and development of wide-field polarimetric calibration procedures. VSTPOL will open a new domain of survey-scale optical polarimetry.

Items.Authors: Naoki Kohara, Yoshinori Suematsu, Toshihiro Tsuzuki, Hideki Takami, Kozo Hayata, Tadahito Mizutani
Items.Title: Wavefront metrology concept for the convex secondary mirror of a large optical segmented space telescope
Items.Abstract: Earth observation from geostationary orbit is expected to play a significant role in disaster mitigation, infrastructure monitoring, and other societal applications. To achieve high-resolution imaging, we are developing technologies for a 3.6 m class optical space telescope with a segmented primary mirror.  One of the most technically demanding challenges is high-accuracy wavefront metrology of the large convex secondary mirror, mounted on its support structure in a telescope integration and test environment. To meet the optical performance goal, measurement error must be within 10 nm RMS. However, the technical difficulty is very high, and conventional approaches using null optics or large spherical mirrors are costly.  In this presentation, we discuss candidate measurement methods and our metrology approaches using stitching techniques. We present measurement error estimates based on simulation and experimental data and describe the conceptual design of the proposed measurement system.

Items.Authors: Domenico Bonaccini Calia, Kathryn E. Hartley, David R. Jenkins, James Osborn
Items.Title: Wavefront modal spatio-temporal coherence in turbulent atmospheres
Items.Abstract: We present our ongoing activities to study the spatio-temporal coherence of atmospheric turbulence, for different atmosphere strengths. The research aims at understanding and modelling the modal angular anisoplanatism and their respective power spectra as a function of the angular distance between two sources.     The work is linked to our team research on the use of the propagation delay method to retrieve the tip-tilt from the LGS. The aim is to explore the adaptive optics correction of tip-tilt and focus using the Laser Guide Star (LGS) signal, one of the holy grails for astronomy and, even more, for optical feeder links in satellite optical communications.     The ongoing numerical simulations methods, the flowing results and the experimental validation will be highlighted. The perspectives of machine-learning tip-tilt control will be outlined.

Items.Authors: Laurent A. Pueyo, Iva Laginja, Rémi Soummer, Nicolas Flagey, Laura Coyle, Tyler McCracken, Emiel Por
Items.Title: What is a residual speckle? An answer with analytical modeling of contrast stability
Items.Abstract: In this paper we discuss the statistics of systematic noise (aka speckles) in high-contrast imaging. We start from first principles and derive the probability density function of speckles stemming from various misalignments (wavefront errors or others) in an astronomical observatory equipped with a coronagraph instrument in various cases.We show that this theoretical formalism matches very well diffractive end-to-end simulations of a few possible instrument configurations of the Habitable Worlds Observatory. We then consider the case of normally distributed wavefront errors and show how this formalism simplifies into a concise analytical model that ties together contrast stability, coronagraph sensitivities (calculated using said diffractive models), and wavefront variance. We demonstrate that this analytical model matches very well end-to-end simulations of hypothetical HWO exoplanet observations that use differential imaging for signal discrimination.

Items.Authors: Yahel Sofer Rimalt, Sagi Ben-Ami, Eran Ofek, David Polishook, Regev Klein, Oren Ironi, Ofir Hershko, Alex Bichkovsky, Arie Blumenzweig, Na'ama Hallakoun, Yossi Shvartzvald, Itzik Filizer, Kyler Kuehn, Stephen Levine, Amanda Bosh, Gerard Van Belle, Ben Hardesty, Tom Bida, Ryan Hamilton
Items.Title: WILDS: a high-efficiency, broadband, medium-resolution workhorse spectrograph for the Lowell Discovery Telescope
Items.Abstract: The Weizmann Institute Lowell Discovery Spectrograph (WILDS) is a new medium-resolution (R ≈ 4000), multi-arm, long-slit spectrograph for the 4.3-m Lowell Discovery Telescope (LDT). Designed to replace the DeVeny spectrograph, WILDS offers simultaneous wavelength coverage from 310 to 915 nm using a unique six-arm, two-detector architecture. Each arm employs an ion-etched transmission grating, whose unit-cell profile is optimized to maximize throughput, functioning as the sole dispersive element. Inspired by the SoXS spectrograph, the WILDS design delivers seeing-limited image quality and broad bandpass coverage using first-order gratings, avoiding the complexity and throughput losses of an echelle. A 1.5′ slit and a full-band atmospheric dispersion corrector (ADC) enable efficient spectroscopy of extended sources across a wide range of observing conditions. I will present the optical concept of the spectrograph and front end, and summarize expected performance and project status.

Items.Authors: John A. Booth
Items.Title: Wrapping metal around glass: Why is opto-mechanical engineering design so hard?
Items.Abstract: Opto-mechanical engineering design can be described in its simplest terms as “wrapping metal around glass”. In a completed optical design, the optics appear to float in space, in perfect alignment with each other. All that remains for the opto-mechanical designer to do is support the optical components, with appropriate adjustment capability, in the desired configuration. But problems abound. Optics are fragile, expensive, and take a relatively long time to procure. Normal engineering materials are typically not good thermal matches for the optics they support. Fine adjustment capability is often in conflict with a system’s requirements for high mechanical stability. And as a niche discipline at the intersection of mechanical engineering and optical design, there are relatively few capable, experienced designers, and even fewer potential mentors. In this paper, we explore some of the problems associated with opto-mechanical design, and discuss potential solutions.

Items.Authors: Kjetil Dohlen, Dimitri Buffat, Will Saunders, Andrea Bianco, Olaf Iwert, Liz George, Etienne Burtin, Roland Bacon, David Lee, Roelof de Jong, Laurence Tresse
Items.Title: WST, the Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope: design trade-offs for the low-resolution multi-object spectrograph instrument
Items.Abstract: The Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope (WST) is a planned 12-meter-class dedicated spectroscopic facility designed to address key scientific challenges through large spectroscopic surveys. This paper presents design and performance trade-offs for the Low-Resolution Multi-Object Spectrograph (MOS-LR) instrument. With a multiplex of 30 000, this instrument will provide unprecedented survey efficiency, an order of magnitude beyond current facilities. Covering the 370 to 980 nm range at a resolving power of 3000 with a sky-projected fiber diameter of 1’’, this instrument faces extreme design, manufacturing, and maintenance challenges. We report on the systematic approach taken to trade off optical and mechanical design options, taking into account constraints such as volume and mass, but also projected availability of detectors and gratings etc.

Items.Authors: Stuart Whittley, Lewis Ball, Naomi McClure-Griffiths
Items.Title: A new era in radio astronomy: the progress of the Square Kilometre Array Observatory
Items.Abstract: The SKAO is a global collaboration of Member States whose mission is to build and operate the two most advanced radio telescope networks on Earth to transform our understanding of the Universe, and deliver benefits to society through global collaboration and innovation.   The SKAO is advancing through a key phase of construction and system integration as work progresses on SKA-Low in Australia and SKA-Mid in South Africa. This presentation provides an update on the Observatory’s technical progress, highlighting recent integration milestones and early performance indicators from both telescopes. We outline the evolving approaches to verification, commissioning, and operations planning that are shaping the path toward Early Science. Key challenges associated with scaling to full observatory capability and an overview of the forthcoming steps that will lead the SKAO from construction into routine scientific observation later in the decade are discussed.

Items.Authors: David A. Henderson, Qin Xu
Items.Title: A novel R-θ fiber positioner for Spec-S5 spectroscopic telescopes
Items.Abstract: The ambitiously proposed next generation spectroscopy survey Spec-S5 and other science programs require significant technological advances in smaller and higher-density fiber positioner modules. We present a novel architecture that replaces the θ–Φ mechanism with an R–θ fiber-motion system driven by direct-drive Squiggle® piezoelectric motors, thereby eliminating gears, backlash, and associated reliability issues. This R-θ design features reduced fiber twist and simplified collision avoidance algorithms when compared with θ-Φ design, smaller fiber defocus (due to smaller patrol radius), stationary electrical wires for both the rotary and linear motors, angle and linear sensors integrated for closed-loop control, operating at ≤ 12V, and calibrated drive and control electronics below each positioner within the 6.2 mm spacing. The R-θ design concept, its key features, and the performance results from subassembly testing are presented.

Items.Authors: Manxuan Zhang, Maxwell Millar-Blanchaer, Briley L. Lewis, Eduardo Marin, William Melby, Michael P. Fitzgerald, Dimitri Mawet, Keith Matthews, Nemanja Jovanovic, Scott Lilley, Edward Wetherell, Jacob Taylor, Mahawa Cisse, Lauren Simmons, Paul Richards, Carlos Alvarez, Jim Lyke, Percy Gomez, Jacques-Robert Delorme, Trisha Hammen, Jayke Nguyen
Items.Title: Enabling infrared polarimetry for Keck NIRC2
Items.Abstract: The Keck/NIRC2 infrared imager was upgraded in 2025 with a new suite of polarimetric observing modes. The new modes enabled by the upgrade span the 1.1 to 4.1 μm range (J through L’ bands) and include imaging polarimetry, coronagraphic imaging polarimetry, and spectropolarimetry with both natural and laser guide star adaptive optics. The mode consists of two half-wave plate modulators (one for J/H/K and one for L’), and a downstream Wollaston prism. The half-wave plates have been thoroughly characterized in our lab with a dual-rotating retarder polarimeter, and commissioning observations were performed October 2025 to January 2026. We present the new mode’s capabilities, polarimetric accuracy, calibration steps, preliminary science results, technical next steps, and future potential science cases. The polarimetry upgrade opens up a wide range of new studies, including investigations of exoplanets, the Galactic center, active galactic nuclei, and the solar system.

Items.Authors: Steffen Mieske
Items.Title: ESO science operations: from the VLT to the ELT
Items.Abstract: ESO’s Paranal Observatory has been operating the Very Large Telescope (VLT) as a mature, highly efficient facility and is now preparing for the arrival of the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). The Paranal Science Operations is an integral part of ESO's end-to-end data flow process. In this presentation we will review how the science operations of the VLT has evolved in the last decade to effectively and efficiently deliver highest quality data to our users. The contribution will outline the changes we have applied to operational concepts & processes to reach the current level of performance. We will present our key operational metrics, discuss their evolution and the lessons learnt from this. We will also summarise the science operations concept foreseen for the ELT, whose operations will be integrated into the evolving VLT system and shall be considered as 'one telescope more'.

Items.Authors: Christopher B. Mendillo
Items.Title: First flight results from PICTURE-D, a NASA balloon mission to directly image debris disks
Items.Abstract: PICTURE-D is a NASA high-altitude balloon mission to directly image exoplanetary systems with the goal of characterizing the inner debris disks of several nearby stars in reflected visible light. The observatory performed its first balloon flight on October 1, 2025 from the NASA CSBF launch facility in Ft. Sumner, NM. The experiment consists of a 60 cm off-axis telescope coupled with a coronagraph instrument containing high and low-order wavefront control systems, dual BMC MEMS deformable mirrors and a charge 6 vector vortex focal plane mask. During the 20 hour flight, 4 stars were observed: Vega, Altair, Fomalhaut and the Gamma Cassiopeiae binary system. On-sky contrast was limited to the 1e-6 level due to poor EFC dark hole convergence and residual pointing jitter owing to a throughput issue with one of the low-order wavefront sensors. We present the observational results from the flight and a description of the technical performance of the observatory sub-systems.

Items.Authors: Max E. Charles, Benjamin Pope, Louis Desdoigts, Jonah Goldfine, Peter G. Tuthill
Items.Title: Image reconstruction with the JWST interferometer
Items.Abstract: The performance of the Aperture Masking Interferometer (AMI) on the NIRISS instrument on board JWST was found to be limited by non-linear detector systematics, particularly charge migration. Conventional interferometric Fourier observables used in most current image reconstruction methods are hence degraded, resulting in severe PSF miscalibration artefacts. Building on the end-to-end differentiable forward model & calibration code amigo, we present a regularized maximum-likelihood (RML) image reconstruction framework. Here we present infrared imaging results on three high contrast protoplanetary disk targets. To image reliably at the diffraction limit, we also train a machine learning model on a suite of images of protoplanetary disk systems to create a lower-dimensionality latent space. The image reconstruction is then performed in this latent space which encodes prior knowledge of protoplanetary disks in general, and these results are compared to the RML approach.

Items.Authors: Gordon J. Stacey, POEMM Team
Items.Title: POEMM: the planetary origins and evolution multi-spectral monochromator
Items.Abstract: POEMM is a 1.8-meter balloon-borne telescope under development as a NASA Astrophysics Pioneers Mission. Leveraging new VIPA spectrometer and absorber-coupled MKID technologies POEMM promises unprecedented sensitivity at high spectral resolving power in the far-IR. POEMM is optimized to study the evolution of protoplanetary disks into planetary systems through velocity resolving low-lying HD and water vapor rotational transitions, and the 63 μm [OI] line which tomographically reveals the distribution of disk mass, the thermochemistry of cool water vapor, and the energy balance within disks as a function of radial distance from the central star, with sub-AU precision. POEMM's grating spectrometer will measure the largely unexplored solid-state water ice emission features at 43, 47, and 62 μm, measuring ice mass. POEMM will be launched from McMurdo during the Austral summer of 2029-2030. This presentation provides an overview of science, technology, instrument design and mission profile.

Items.Authors: Bogdan Jeram, Petr Chatrny, Robert Donaldson, Josef Hofer, Arturo Hoffstadt Urrutia, Linus Karl, Nick Kornweibel, Calle Rosenquist, Marcos Suárez Valles, Artur Szostak
Items.Title: RTC toolkit: ESO's solution to address challenges of implementing new-generation RTCs
Items.Abstract: The RTC toolkit is a software solution developed by the European Southern Observatory (ESO) to address challenges in implementing advanced Adaptive Optics Real-Time Controllers (AO RTCs). It's primarily designed to realize RTCs for the Extremely Large Telescope's (ELT) instruments, but it is also applicable for future Very Large Telescope (VLT) AO instruments. The software toolkit is flexible and can accommodate diverse needs and requirements in terms of scalability and performance. Its introduction aims to streamline implementation efforts, foster commonality among RTC implementations, and tackle future maintenance and obsolescence concerns. The paper explores the architecture, implementation, and performance aspects of the toolkit, and provides the current status of the development and its usage.

Items.Authors: Hongbang Liu, Zuke Feng, Lirong Xie, Huanbo Feng, Huijun Hu, Difan Yi, Fei Xie, Yanjun Xie, Zongwang Fan, Jin Zhang, Wenjin Xie, Xuefeng Huang, Wei Deng, Dong Wang, Zili Li, Hui Wang, Ran Chen, Shiqiang Zhou, Kai Chen, Jin Li, Qian Liu, Shi Chen, Zhenyu Tang, Hangzhou Li, Bo Peng, Shulin Liu, Xiangming Sun, Yangheng Zheng, Enwei Liang, Lian Tao, Lizhi Sheng, Liang Sun, Fei Ding, Yong Yang, Yanji Yang
Items.Title: SXPE: swift X-ray polarization experiment
Items.Abstract: The Swift X-ray Polarization Experiment (SXPE) is a rapid-response microsatellite mission dedicated to soft X-ray polarimetry of high-energy transient sources. X-ray polarization provides a unique diagnostic of emission geometry, magnetic-field configuration, and radiation processes in extreme astrophysical environments. However, current missions such as IXPE and the future eXTP lack the agility required for prompt follow-up of fast-evolving transients including gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) and X-ray binary outbursts. SXPE is designed to fill this gap by enabling minute-scale autonomous repointing to triggers from wide-field monitors. SXPE consists of a lightweight Wolter-I focusing X-ray telescope, a high-sensitivity Gas Microchannel Plate Detector (GMPD), a high-deployment-ratio extendable boom, and an agile microsatellite platform. Items.Authors: Yann Clénet, Vincent Lapeyrère, Eric Gendron, Fabrice Vidal, Frédéric Chapron, Mathieu Cohen, Sylvain Guieu, Roderick Dembet, Eric Meyer, Arnaud Sevin, Fanny Chemla, Olivier Dupuis, Kévin Cloiseau, Gilles Fasola, Karim Hussein, Sylvain Isambert, Gaudemard Julien, Florian Ferreira, Hervé Locatelli, Nicolas Gautherot, Antonin Poyard, Lahoucine Ghouchou, Emmanuel Tisserand, Alexandre Blin, Labasse Berthe, Srilakshmi Ramalingam, Claude Collin, Julian Porras, Nicolas Levraud, Caroline Kulcsár, Henri-François Raynaud, Sassolas Benoît, Laurent Pinard, Christophe Michel, Cyrille Blanchard, Ihsan Ibn Taïeb, William Wang, Samir Mairia, Tristan Buey, Jordan Raffard, Vincent Chevalier, Sylvestre Taburet, Dalia Djetten, François Meyer, Pierre Baudoz, Elsa Huby, Sebastian Rabien, Eckhard Sturm, Richard Davies
Items.Title: The MICADO first light imager for the ELT: the SCAO module AIT in France, from the beta flat configuration towards the flat and final configurations
Items.Abstract: MICADO is the ELT first light imager, working at the diffraction limit of the telescope thanks to a SCAO and an MCAO mode. Since summer 2024, MICADO is in its AIT phase and all MICADO partners are currently integrating their subsystems. The MICADO SCAO module will follow three successive AIT phases in France: the beta flat configuration, the flat configuration and the final configuration.   In this contribution I will first present the progress made in the AIT of the beta flat configuration and its closed loop results. I will then present the performed and on-going tasks to prepare the flat and final configurations (manufacturing, delivery and integration of several SCAO subsystems) and the results obtained so far in the flat configuration. I will then conclude with the expected following steps until the delivery of the SCAO module at MPE for its integration with the other MICADO subsystems.

Items.Authors: Richard T. Demers, Fernando Quirós-Pacheco, Bo Xin, Arielle Bertrou-Cantou, Juan Pablo Haddad, Jordi Molgo, Paulo Silva, Josema Filgueira, Marianne Cox, Marcos van Dam, Dan Catropa, Jan Kansky, Brian McLeod, Andrew Cline, Cedric Plantet, Alfio Pulgisi, Fabio Rossi, Nicolo Azzaroli, Simone Esposito, Rob Sharp, Noelia Martinez-Rey, Tony Travouillon, Bijan Nemati, Guillermo Gonzalez, Thiago Amaral, Rafael Ribeiro, Patrick Reardon, Damien Jones
Items.Title: Adaptive optics advancement at the Giant Magellan Telescope
Items.Abstract: The adaptive optics system is the keystone for attaining high image quality in an extremely large segmented-aperture telescope like the Giant Magellan Telescope. We report on the significant progress in the development of wavefront sensors and control algorithms for the two diffraction-limited AO observation modes on the Giant Magellan Telescope. The GMT wavefront sensing and control suite of subsystems comprises three wavefront sensors, an Adaptive Optics Test Camera for verification of AO control algorithm and a laser guide star facility for carrying out laser tomographic atmospheric correction. We have advanced the designs of all of these subsystems.    We have invested strategically in testbeds and prototypes to de-risk the designs and the control strategies. We have recently built the GAPS (GMT Adaptive Optics and Phasing Sensor) testbed to test and verify performance of the NGAO (Natural Guide Star AO) mode. We have also advanced the LTAO mode by testing hardware prototypes.

Items.Authors: Maxime Rombach, Markus Thurneysen, Jurgen Schmoll, Diane Chapuis, Malak Galal, Sébastien Pernecker, Jean-Paul Kneib, Michaela Hirschmann
Items.Title: MOSAIC at ELT: design and first performance results of novel robotic optical-relay positioners
Items.Abstract: MOSAIC, a multi-object spectrograph for the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT), will fully exploit the telescope’s unprecedented collecting area using 261 robotic positioners that accurately pick off light from the curved focal surface and deliver it to near-infrared (NIR) and visible (VIS) spectrographs. Given the scale of the ELT, the positioners incorporate compact optical relays to re-image sub-fields onto two fixed fiber bundles located 600 mm behind the focal plane, adjust to the local telecentricity to accurately point toward the ELT pupil 37.8 m away, and include individual atmospheric dispersion correction to mitigate wavelength-dependent image shifts across the focal surface. In this paper, we present the conceptual design, mechanical and optical prototyping, and the first laboratory performance results of the MOSAIC positioners.

Items.Authors: Herman L. Marshall, Sarah Heine, Alan Garner, Ralf Heilmann, Stephen Bongiorno, Andrea Santangelo, Christoph Tenzer, Eric Gullikson, Hans M. Guenther, Swati Ravi
Items.Title: A new NASA Pioneer: the globe orbiting soft X-ray polarimeter (GOSoX)
Items.Abstract: The Globe Orbiting Soft X-ray Polarimeter (GOSoX) is a spectropolarimeter for the soft X-ray band. GOSoX is based on the Rocket Experiment Demonstration of a Soft X-ray Polarimeter (REDSoX), a NASA-funded sounding rocket payload. Like REDSoX, GOSoX consists of Wolter I X-ray optics from MSFC, Critical Angle Transmission (CAT) gratings made at MIT, and multilayer (ML) coated mirrors that polarize the X-rays from LBNL. Colleagues at U. Tuebingen will adapt commercially available sCMOS sensors for the focal plane. The grating dispersion is matched to the lateral grading of ML mirrors set at 45deg. GOSoX can measure polarization across the entire 0.2-0.4 keV band with a spectral resolution E/dE ~ 100. Minimum detectable polarizations (MDPs) of 3-10% are expected for over a dozen targets in a one-year mission. The mission was proposed to the NASA call for Astrophysics Pioneers in 2025. The mission was rated "selectable"; pending available funds in the FY26 NASA budget.

Items.Authors: Nicole Melso, David Schiminovich, Erika Hamden
Items.Title: Integral field spectropolarimetry with the Circumgalactic Ha Spectrograph (CHaS)
Items.Abstract: We aim to enable integral field spectropolarimetry with the Circumgalactic Hα Spectrograph (CHαS), leveraging  the low-surface brightness sensitivity and high velocity resolution of CHαS to map the  spatio-kinematic properties of dust grains in/around nearby galaxies using polarized optical line emission.  Polarized light traces the large-scale dust distribution, the properties of dust grains aligned in magnetic  fields, and the processes that transport metal-enriched material far into the halo. In  a few hours of observations, CHαS will produce velocity-resolved maps of the dust  distribution in bright nebulae targets detected in polarized line emission. Our  longer-term efforts to push CHαS towards fainter sensitivity limits stand to yield the deepest emission-line maps  of linear and circular polarization ever produced. We will present the CHαS spectropolarimetry design and expected performance, and discuss its potential as a testbed for new technologies including polarizing metasurfaces.

Items.Authors: Karwan Rostem
Items.Title: POEMM: an overview of the design and performance expectation of the science instrument element
Items.Abstract: The Planetary Origins and Evolution Multispectral Monochromator (POEMM) is a 1.8-meter balloon-borne far-infrared telescope recently selected as a NASA Astrophysics Pioneers Mission. POEMM is designed to directly probe the evolution of protoplanetary disks. The POEMM science instrument element (SIE) has three spectrometer modules: (i) HR1 is designed to achieve velocity-resolved measurements of the HD J=1-0 emission at 112µm with R~100,000; (ii) HR2 will selectively observe four spectral lines at R~50,000: two water vapor transitions at 40.69 and 46.48 µm, the HD J=2-1 line at 56.23 µm and the [OI] 63.18 µm line; (iii) LR, a grating spectrometer, will cover 35-70 µm and the important broadband water-ice features at 43 and 63 µm. In this presentation, we provide an overview of the SIE cryostat design, spectrometer modules, optical layout, and expected sensitivity. POEMM is scheduled for launch in the Austral 2029-2030 summer.

Items.Authors: Julien Drevon, Margaux Abello, Florentin Millour, Anthony Meilland, Armando Domiciano
Items.Title: PYRA and MYTHRA: new statistical analysis for image reconstruction
Items.Abstract: Optical interferometry combined with 4 beam-combiner instruments achieves sub-milliarcsecond resolution using the VLTI, allowing detailed imaging of complex astrophysical environments. Reconstructing such images from interferometric observables like visibilities and closure phases requires sophisticated algorithms such as the one provided in the MiRA, SQUEEZE, IRBis, and SPARCO. However, statistical assessment of reconstructed images remains challenging.  We present PYRA and MYTHRA, two Python wrappers designed to make image reconstruction analysis more intuitive, automated, and statistically robust. These tools combine multiple reconstructions to produce a final statistically weighted image, enabling reliable confirmation of observed structures. PYRA/MYTHRA drastically reduce analysis time (from weeks to under an hour) and are now official MiRA companion tools, already adopted in several published studies.

Items.Authors: Rico Landman, David Doelman, Jeroen Rietjens, Iva Laginja, Pierre Baudoz, Kristien Peeters, Chris van Dijk, Yuki Nishie, Yuta Watanabe, Joost van den Born, Alexander Eigenraam, Mario Vretenar, Mariya Krasteva, Matteo Taccola, Frans Snik
Items.Title: SUPPPPRESS: developing low-leakage liquid-crystal vector vortex coronagraphs for space-based exoplanet imaging
Items.Abstract: We report on the ESA-funded SUPPPPRESS project, focused on developing high-performance liquid-crystal coronagraphs for the direct detection and spectral characterization of Earth-like exoplanets. The goal is to improve the contrast and operational spectral bandwidth of the Vector Vortex Coronagraph (VVC). We manufacture regular and multi-grating VVCs (mgVVCs), stacking two or three liquid-crystal masks (LCMs) with vortex and grating patterns to mitigate polarization leakage. This enables full exploitation of the VVC's achromatic and scale-invariant properties. We detail the improved manufacturing of LCMs by ColorLink Japan, Ltd. and their quality assessment using far-field diffraction, polarization microscopy, and zero-order leakage spectroscopy. The individual LCMs are assembled into mgVVCs using a custom jig. We demonstrate their broadband contrast performance on the THD2 testbed, comparing standard VVCs and mgVVCs. Finally, we discuss space environmental qualification of the masks.

Items.Authors: Jörg Weingrill, Thomas Granzer, Arto S. Järvinen
Items.Title: Telescope acquisition and guiding using TwinCAT vision
Items.Abstract: We use a GigE vision camera mounted on an auxiliary telescope on RoboTel and the STELLA telescopes to improve the acquisition of the telescope position. The main advantage to use TwinCAT vision is to shortcut the Java telescope control system, which vastly improves the correction cycles. We first tested the implementation on the 80-cm RoboTel telescope. As it turned out, the main caveat for proper acquisition of the telescope position on sky is the flexture of the main mirror. While acquisition works for the azimuthal mounted aux telescope, guiding is not advantageous. A future implementation shall include the guiding using the off-axis camera inside the main camera housing to achieve sub arc second precision.

Items.Authors: Gordon J. Stacey, CCAT Team
Items.Title: CCAT the Fred Young Submillimeter Telescope (FYST) nears first light on Cerro Chajnantor: status and first light science
Items.Abstract: The CCAT Consortium has funded the Fred Young Submillimeter Telescope (FYST), a 6-meter aperture wide field of view telescope sited at 5600 m elevation near the summit of Cerro Chajnantor in northern Chile. The telescope properties, its site, and its state-of-the-art instrumentation promises unrivaled mapping speed for (sub)mm-wave surface brightness studies ranging from Big Bang cosmology through reionization and the assembly of the first galaxies and on to star formation in the Milky Way.     FYST is nearing completion on Chajnantor and will be sequentially receiving its first light instrumentation, a submm heterodyne receiver (MiniCHAI) and a wide-field direct detection receiver (Prime-Cam) for first light in mid-2026. This talk will include a brief review of the overall science objectives addressed with FYST, the current state of the instrumentation and telescope, and finish with a discussion of the first light and early science programs that we plan for the 2026 season.

Items.Authors: Johannes Wüthrich, Banan Yamani, Andrin Fazan, Léonard Lebrun, Sean MacBride, Felipe Andrade-Oliveira, Marcelle Soares-Santos, Guandi Zhao
Items.Title: Characterizing robotic positioners under the influence of changing gravity vectors for future spectroscopic surveys
Items.Abstract: Future spectroscopic surveys will rely on highly multiplexed focal planes composed of robotic fiber positioners. To ensure science goals are met, a stringent testing of these positioners is of utmost importance during prototyping and quality assurance. We present a dynamical telescope simulator test stand, to characterize the positioners in terms of position, focus and angular tilt stability under the variation of the gravity vector. We discuss the design and characterization of our test stand including reference measurements with a robotic positioner from the SDSS-V experiment. Finally we present initial results with a prototype positioner module built by Orbray Co., Ltd. This setup offers an important platform for integrated testing of advanced focal-plane technologies in operations-like conditions.

Items.Authors: Nazim Ali Bharmal, Raziye Artan, David G. Bramall, Ben Buky, Tim Butterley, Polly Gill, Joel Harman, David King, Jennifer King, Tim Morris, Phil Parr-Burman, Jürgen Schmoll, Noah Schwartz, Patrick Smith
Items.Title: MOSAIC at ELT: delivering a GLAO-corrected and distortion-aware 8 arcminute field
Items.Abstract: MOSAIC is the MOS & IFU for the ELT over the 7.8 arcminute diameter field. Achieving sufficient coupling of light into ca.300 apertures spread across the field, accounting for wavefront compensation and measurement of apertures positioning to focal plane distortions is a key performance metric. The GLAO subsystem delivers measurements and control signals for these goals using three types of sources (NGS, LGS, and on-instrument point sources) and we review the opto-mechanical and control designs, implementation considerations and the AITV perspectives for verification.
